questions.prompt: A server in Virginia (UTC−5) runs at 01:00 UTC on 15 December. A function uses `new Date().getDate()`. Which day does it report?
options: It depends on the browser
questions.why: getDate uses the machine's zone: in Virginia it is still 20:00 on the 14th.

wrong.0: 15 is the UTC date, and the school's date. getDate does not use either.
wrong.1: No zone is that far ahead of Virginia.
wrong.3: This code runs on the server. No browser is involved.

options: An error
questions.why: JavaScript rolls the two extra days into March. It does not refuse.

wrong.0: 30 February cannot be kept: no such day exists.
wrong.2: Date does not refuse; it rolls over silently. That is the trap.
wrong.3: It is not clamped to the end of the month.

questions.prompt: A term runs 2026-09-14 to 2026-12-18. Is 2026-12-18 in the term?
options: Yes: both ends are included
No: the end is not included
Only until noon
Only if it is a weekday
questions.why: The last day of term is a school day. Compare with <= on both ends.

wrong.1: That would cut the last school day off.
wrong.2: A calendar date has no hours.
wrong.3: Weekdays are not part of the rule.

questions.prompt: Why can `"2026-09-14" < "2026-12-18"` be trusted as a date comparison?
options: JavaScript turns them into dates first
It cannot be trusted
Because both are 10 characters long
In YYYY-MM-DD form, text order is date order
questions.why: Year, then month, then day, each with fixed digits: comparing text character by character compares the dates.

wrong.0: It compares the text. That works only because of the form.
wrong.1: It can, as long as both are in YYYY-MM-DD form.
wrong.2: Length alone is not enough: "14/12/2026" is 10 characters too, and sorts wrongly.

questions.prompt: GPIS D-247: does the query `asante g.` match "Godfred Kofi Asante"?
options: No: the words are in the wrong order
No: because of the full stop
No: "g" is not a whole word
Yes
questions.why: Every typed word appears in the name, in any order, and full stops are ignored.

wrong.0: Order does not matter in D-247.
wrong.2: A typed word only has to appear somewhere in the name.

questions.prompt: GPIS D-247: does the query `ama mensah` match "Ama Serwaa Birikran"?
options: No: "mensah" is not in the name
Yes: one matching word is enough
Yes, on the first name only
An error
questions.why: Every typed word must appear in the name. "mensah" does not.

wrong.1: D-247 needs every word, not one.
wrong.3: A search never errors because of a name.

questions.prompt: Find the mistake in a unit test: `function isToday(d) { return d === schoolToday(); }`
options: `===` cannot compare text
It reads the real clock, so the result depends on the day the test runs
It should use `==`
Nothing is wrong
questions.why: schoolToday() with no argument reads the clock. Pass a fixed moment instead.

wrong.2: `==` would change nothing here, and is never better.
wrong.3: The test would pass on one day and fail on the next.

questions.why: trim leaves "Ama   Birikran". Splitting on one space gives "Ama", "", "", "Birikran".

wrong.0: The three spaces between the words give two empty pieces.
wrong.1: Count the pieces between three spaces: there are two empty ones.
wrong.3: trim removed the spaces at both ends first.
